## The MNL model

$$
\Pr(i_{nit} \mid \beta) = \frac{\exp(\beta X_{nit})}{\sum_{j=1}^{J}\exp(\beta X_{njt})}
$$

where

- $\beta$ is a vector of parameters to be estimated
- $X_{nit}$ are the levels of the attributes

## Another frame with some equations

$$
\begin{split}
  \int_2^4\frac{1}{x^2}dx &= \int_2^4 x^{-2}dx\\
  &= \left[\frac{1}{-2+1}x^{-2 + 1}\right]_2^4\\
  &= \left[-\frac{1}{x}\right]_2^4\\
  &= -\tfrac{1}{4} - \left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right)\\
  &= -\tfrac{1}{4} + \tfrac{1}{2}\\
  &= \tfrac{1}{4}
\end{split}
$$

# Results from R

## Code shown on a slide

```{r}
#| echo: true
model <- lm(dist ~ speed, data = cars)
coef(model)
```

## Regression output as a table

```{r}
model <- lm(dist ~ speed, data = cars)
estimates <- summary(model)$coefficients
knitr::kable(estimates, digits = 3)
```

## Stopping distance rises with speed

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars, aes(speed, dist)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  labs(x = "Speed (mph)", y = "Stopping distance (ft)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## A plot next to text

:::: {.columns align=center}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 3
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +

```
